text:
sam: infra alert — seeing 4 KV-cache OOMs in the last 10m on gpu-pool-a. all during >8k token conversations. stack traces look like allocation spikes when merging new KV pages. attaching quick logs and pprof snapshot.
infra-bot: [ALERT] kv-cache:oom pool=gpu-pool-a node=gpux-12 region=us-west-2 count=4
sam: logs (snip):\n```
2026-03-17T22:13:02Z WARN runtime: kv-page-alloc failed: out of memory, requested=128Mi slab_remain=12Mi
2026-03-17T22:13:02Z ERROR serve: request id=rq_42 failed after 312ms: kv_alloc OOM
```
julia: can you paste the pprof heap growth diff? need to see whether fragments are leftover vs a steady linear grow
sam: pprof diff (top lines):\n```
+87.1Mi  23.4%  23.4%  87.1Mi  23.4%  kv/pagemanager.(*Page).Allocate
+64.0Mi  17.2%  40.6%  64.0Mi  17.2%  kv/cache.(*Shard).retainPage
```
matt: looks like retainPage isn't releasing on reuse path — probably a refcount leak when a page is partially consumed and then reinserted. saw similar in the compression/quantization rollout PR.
irene: quick mitigations we can push: 1) aggressive slab compaction on low free pressure, 2) soft-fallback to short-context model variant (e.g., max_ctx=2048) for affected routes, 3) synchronous drain/evict path before allocating new pages. which is lowest risk? 
sam: order of risk: 2) short-context fallback is lowest (no runtime change), 1) compaction moderate (may add latency spikes), 3) synchronous drain highest risk during tail latency.
julia: we should instrument a fast path metric: "kv_page_reuse_miss" event and add a circuit to stop re-inserting pages that are >75% fragmented. prevents repeated bloat.
matt: provisional plan: feature-flag rollout of a guardrail that refuses to create new large pages if free < X and instead triggers eviction+reuse attempt; fallback to shorter context if eviction fails. I'll sketch a PR.
sam: also found a reproducible micro-repro: run this harness with seeded long-dialog workload, observe fragmentation map growing over 2k steps. snippet: \n```
./tools/kv_harness --pool gpux-12 --seq 8k --reuse=on --threads=16 --report=pprof
```
julia: for quick prod safety, can ops throttle long-context customers? maybe temporarily reduce per-cust max_seq or request fallback at gateway
irene: ops can add a rate-limit rule per api-key tied to long-context token window. I'll coordinate with support to notify impacted customers.
infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-234; paging oncall: @matt
matt: starting a short-lived canary: add guard that when slab_free < 32Mi then switch worker to "compact-first" eviction strategy and enable reuse_miss metric. rolling to 10% now.
sam: can we also add a low-latency async reclaimer thread that consolidates fragmented pages during idle CPU cycles? low risk and helps long-run growth
julia: yes but need careful race handling with per-request alloc path. if we gate it behind a global lock it'll hurt tail latency. prefer lock-free per-shard reclamation with CAS on page headers.
matt: agreed. short-term: canary metrics look good, no extra OOMs in 30m. I'll open PR with feature flag + tests + e2e repro harness. PR will include the following TODOs: add metric, guard threshold, fallback routing change, async compactor.
sam: thanks. follow-up: schedule a 20m sync tomorrow to review PR and decide thresholds for prod flip. :thumbsup:
